brief.headline: Memory supercycle locks in: DRAM/NAND up 58-75% QoQ, HBM4 ramps collide with $700B hyperscaler sprint
brief.summary: <cite index="15-2,15-7">DRAM contract prices surged 58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026 while NAND jumped 70-75%, following Q1's 90-95% DRAM spike.</cite> <cite index="1-2,1-8">HBM demand is exploding from hyperscaler AI buildouts including OpenAI Stargate and China's DeepSeek, keeping supply red-hot.</cite> <cite index="19-1,19-3,19-5">Hyperscalers hit $700B in 2026 capex: Alphabet spent $35.67B in Q1 alone (up 2x YoY), Meta raised full-year to $125-145B citing higher component pricing.</cite> <cite index="27-1,27-3">TSMC CoWoS capacity reaches 115-140K wafers/month by end-2026, expanding to ~170K in 2027.</cite> <cite index="42-5,44-5">Samsung began mass production of industry-first HBM4 (11.7Gbps, up to 13Gbps) for NVIDIA Vera Rubin, expects HBM sales to triple in 2026.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="34-1,34-15,34-16">Samsung/SK Hynix buying now comprises 45.6% of daily KOSPI volume (up from 14.7% YoY), with combined market cap at 54.6% of the index.</cite> <cite index="36-1,39-11,39-12,39-14">SK Hynix briefly hit 2 quadrillion won ($1.3T) market cap; gap to Samsung narrowed to 2.5x from historical 5-7x range—tightest ever.</cite> <cite index="39-6,39-7,39-8,39-10">Foreigners poured 3.1T won into SK Hynix over 4 days while Samsung saw zero top-20 net buying.</cite> SK Hynix is the pure HBM play riding GPU/AI server memory, while Samsung's foundry/logic drag dilutes the memory thesis. Short-term pair: long SK Hynix vs. Samsung on HBM4 production lead and allocation certainty. Samsung's HBM4 first-to-market claim needs Nvidia/AMD revenue confirmation—volume ramp timing vs. SK Hynix M15X 1b node is the Q3 catalyst.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="2-13">Q1 2026 memory prices surged 80-90% QoQ across most segments per Counterpoint.</cite> <cite index="5-1,5-2,5-5">DDR4/DDR5 prices more than doubled; some components up 700% vs. historical levels.</cite> <cite index="5-14">Supply partners project potential 10-20% monthly DRAM price increases through end-2026.</cite> <cite index="3-5,3-6">Prices not yet at cycle highs; further upside possible if AI demand doesn't cool, though capacity additions lag market balance.</cite> Structural tailwinds: HBM's 3:1 capacity trade-off vs. DDR5, hyperscaler allocation lock-in, disciplined capex from Big 3. Risk: pricing velocity this steep historically precedes demand destruction or hyperscaler inventory pause.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="42-5,42-6,44-5">Samsung began HBM4 mass production (11.7Gbps consistent, scalable to 13Gbps) using 1c DRAM + 4nm logic die, shipping to customers; expects HBM sales to triple in 2026.</cite> <cite index="46-2,46-3,46-4">Samsung cleared final NVIDIA/AMD HBM4 qualification in Feb, began mass production, with full-scale supply targeted around June for Vera Rubin.</cite> <cite index="48-1,48-2,48-3">Samsung also began shipping industry-first HBM4E samples (14Gbps stable, up to 16Gbps, 3.6TB/s bandwidth) 3 weeks ago.</cite> <cite index="45-4,45-5">Samsung plans 50% HBM capacity ramp in 2026 to ~250K wafers/month (from 170K), converting existing lines + Pyeongtaek P4 expansion.</cite> <cite index="41-7">HBM3E spot prices rose nearly 20% as demand outpaces supply.</cite> <cite index="31-5">NVIDIA secured ~60% of TSMC's 2026 CoWoS capacity (130K wafers/month by year-end).</cite> Samsung's HBM4 first-mover claim is credible but Nvidia allocation share vs. SK Hynix remains opaque—watch for Rubin design-win disclosures at next earnings.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung unveils HBM4 at NVIDIA GTC 2026, ships commercial product
news_pulse.implication: First-to-market positioning in HBM4 (11.7-13Gbps) for Vera Rubin validates Samsung's 1c process node lead; HBM sales triple target depends on NVIDIA allocation vs. SK Hynix split.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM prices +58-63% QoQ in Q2, NAND +70-75% per TrendForce
news_pulse.implication: Contract price momentum accelerates from Q1's 90-95% DRAM jump; Samsung/SK Hynix gross margins inflect sharply in H1—expect 60%+ DRAM GMs by Q2 print.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler AI capex hits $700B in 2026, Meta raises to $125-145B
news_pulse.implication: Meta's capex hike cites higher component costs (memory); validates memory pricing power and de-risks 2H demand even as Amazon FCF collapsed 95%.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix market cap crosses 2 quadrillion won, narrows gap to Samsung to 2.5x
news_pulse.implication: Foreign flow into SK Hynix (3.1T won in 4 days) vs. Samsung snub signals conviction in pure-play HBM exposure; pair trade setup live.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity to reach 115-140K wafers/month by end-2026, 170K in 2027
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS remains HBM bottleneck into 2027; NVIDIA's 60% allocation lock maintains SK Hynix/Samsung supply discipline and pricing.

news_pulse.headline: Memory prices surge 80-90% QoQ in Q1 2026 across segments—Counterpoint
news_pulse.implication: Sharpest QoQ gain on record; Samsung/SK Hynix prioritizing HBM/server DRAM over commodity DDR tightens entire stack—industrial/auto lead times extend to 32-40 weeks.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix account for 45.6% of KOSPI daily buying, up 3x YoY
news_pulse.implication: Index concentration at 54.6% of KOSPI market cap amplifies volatility; any profit-taking ripples across Korean equities—derivatives gamma risk elevated.

news_pulse.headline: VersaLogic warns memory component prices up 700% vs. historical levels
news_pulse.implication: Spot pricing dislocation confirms contract lag; Samsung/SK Hynix contract resets in H2 could deliver another 20-30% step-up into 2027.

brief.derivatives_signal: <cite index="34-1,34-15,34-16">Samsung + SK Hynix now 45.6% of KOSPI daily volume and 54.6% of index market cap, tripling concentration vs. 1 year ago.</cite> Elevated gamma exposure as options dealers hedge binary HBM qualification/allocation headlines. KOSPI 200 futures at-the-money vol likely elevated; any Samsung HBM4 revenue guidance miss or NVIDIA allocation clarity triggers sharp derating. Pair trade via OTC TRS or ADR options (SSNLF/HXSCL) more liquid than KRX single-stock derivatives for non-Korean accounts. Watch for post-earnings vol crush if Samsung confirms Nvidia Rubin volume ramp; otherwise, short-dated calls on SK Hynix vs. Samsung puts captures relative HBM narrative.

KOSPI volatility and derivatives positioning as Samsung/SK Hynix approach 55% of index weight—systematic rebalancing risk
